name: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion® Game of the Year Edition (2009)

Optimal.Notes: A locked 40 fps at 40 Hz gives a smooth, tear-free experience that suits Oblivion's exploration pace well; large textures and HDR restore much of the game's visual character without taxing the GPU. GE-Proton is recommended for best compatibility based on community trends.

profiles.Summary: Oblivion (2009) is a classic RPG that runs well on the Steam Deck via Proton, with the community trending toward platinum status. The game's modest 2009-era PC requirements mean the Deck handles it comfortably at 60 fps with reasonable settings, though some Proton configuration tweaks may be needed for best stability.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the 2009 PC minimum requirements, the game's known engine characteristics, and the Deck's GPU class (roughly GTX 1050 Ti). On first run, check frame rate in an outdoor area like outside the Imperial City — if it drops below your target, reduce Grass Distance and View Distance first, as these are Oblivion's biggest performance levers.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling keeps TDP very low while remaining playable; grass and shadows are the biggest GPU costs in Oblivion and are dialled down here. Refresh rate set to 40 Hz to match the 30 fps cap smoothly.

KnownIssues: Game may require Proton configuration or a compatibility layer tweak to launch correctly — try Proton Experimental or GE-Proton if the default fails.
Mouse cursor can appear during gameplay; using controller input exclusively avoids this.
Some audio issues (crackling or missing sounds) have been reported under Proton — setting audio to 2-channel stereo in-game may help.
Occasional crashes on save/load transitions; keeping saves small and using manual saves frequently is recommended.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Oblivion's 2009-era engine is not particularly demanding and the Deck GPU can push native 1280x800 at high settings; expect dips toward 45 fps in dense outdoor areas with full grass and shadow distance. Drop grass distance to 25% if frame rate dips are noticeable in the wilderness.

Optimal.Notes: A locked 45 fps at 45 Hz gives perfectly smooth, tear-free gameplay that suits Oblivion's pacing well; FSR upscaling from 1024x640 keeps visuals sharp on the OLED screen. Large textures are affordable at this TDP and make the biggest visual difference in this era of game.

profiles.Summary: Oblivion (2009) is a classic, relatively lightweight RPG by modern standards and runs well on the Steam Deck through Proton, with ProtonDB trending platinum suggesting most players get a smooth experience. The aging Gamebryo engine is well within the Deck's capabilities, allowing high settings and solid frame rates without heavy tuning.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's 2009 PC minimum requirements (DirectX 9, 128 MB GPU), ProtonDB's platinum trend, and the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU which vastly exceeds the original spec. On first run, check frame rate in outdoor areas like the Imperial City outskirts — these are the heaviest scenes — and adjust Grass Distance and Object Fade if frame rate dips below your target.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render resolution dropped to 960x600 with FSR upscaling to ease GPU load at a very low TDP; the 2009 Gamebryo engine is CPU-light enough that 5 W TDP is sufficient for most outdoor areas. Shader stutter may appear in the first session but clears up on subsequent plays.

KnownIssues: The game uses DirectX 9 via Proton/DXVK; shader compilation stutters may occur on first play but diminish afterwards.
The in-game launcher may not launch correctly through Proton — starting the game directly (skipping the launcher) is recommended.
Mouse cursor issues or UI scaling quirks may appear when using controller; the game has no official Steam controller profile listed.
Some users report needing to manually configure INI settings (Oblivion.ini) for proper resolution and controller support under Proton.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 at max settings is well within the Deck's reach for this 2009 title; most interior and dungeon areas will hold a solid 60 fps, though dense outdoor areas with high grass distance may dip to the low 50s. Reduce Grass Distance to Medium if dips are bothersome without changing other settings.
